# How to Write a Tailored Cover Letter for One Job Posting Using ChatGPT

> **In short:** Paste one job posting and a short note about your background into ChatGPT with a clear instruction, and you'll get a focused cover letter draft in minutes. The draft is a starting point — you'll still rewrite parts in your own voice before sending.

Staring at a blank page when you need a cover letter is the worst part of applying for a job. The good news: you don't have to start from zero. ChatGPT works like a very fast first-drafter — give it the job post and a few lines about you, and it hands back a structured letter you can shape. This guide walks through that process, one step at a time, so a complete beginner can follow it on a phone or a computer.

## Before you start
- A free ChatGPT account (sign up at chat.openai.com if you don't have one) — a paid plan is not required for this task.
- The job posting copied into a note or kept open in a second tab.
- A few short sentences about yourself — your current role, key experience, and why this job interests you.
- About 10–15 minutes total.

## Step 1 — Open ChatGPT in a fresh conversation

Go to **chat.openai.com** in a browser, or open the ChatGPT app on your phone. If you already have an account, sign in; if not, create one (an email address is enough). Once you're in, look for the **text box at the bottom of the screen** — it's the place you type your message. It's usually labeled something like *Message ChatGPT* or *Ask anything*, but the wording changes sometimes.

If ChatGPT opens an old conversation from a previous session, start a fresh one. Look near the top of the page for a button like a **pencil icon**, a **"+"**, or a **"New chat"** label, and tap it.

💬 Example: Just type **"Hi"** and send it, so you can see how the assistant replies.

You'll know it worked when the assistant greets you back and the text box is empty, ready for your real request.

## Step 2 — Gather two pieces of text in front of you

Before you ask ChatGPT for anything, make sure you can see **the job posting** and **a short summary of your background** — both ready to paste. Open the job listing in one browser tab and either type a few lines about yourself in the Notes app, or open your résumé next to the posting.

What you really need from the job post is: the **job title**, the **main requirements**, and any **keywords that stand out** (for example, "cross-functional teams" or "client-facing"). What you need about yourself is: your **current role**, your **years of experience**, and **one or two achievements** you want to mention.

💬 Example (your background summary): *"I'm a project manager with 6 years in healthcare IT. Led a team of 4. I also volunteer teaching kids to code on weekends. I'm applying because I want to move into renewable energy."*

You'll know it worked when both pieces of text are visible without scrolling, ready to copy.

## Step 3 — Paste both into ChatGPT with a clear instruction

This is the most important step. Click into the **text box at the bottom** of the chat, paste the job posting first, then paste your background summary, then write one clear sentence telling ChatGPT what you want. The clearer you are, the better the draft will be — think of it like giving instructions to a colleague who has never read your résumé.

What you'll see after you press send: your long message appears in the chat, and within a minute or two, a full cover letter draft appears below it. If the message is too long for one box, send the job post first and the rest in a second message.

💬 Example (copy and adapt this prompt):
*"Here's the job I'm applying for: [paste the job post]. Here's a short note about me: [paste your background summary]. Please write a 3-paragraph cover letter that highlights my project management experience and why I want to move into renewable energy. Keep the tone warm but professional."*

You'll know it worked when a structured letter appears in the chat, with an opening paragraph, a middle paragraph about your experience, and a closing paragraph.

## Step 4 — Read the draft and ask for changes that fit you

Don't accept the first draft as final. **Read it slowly**, line by line, and notice what feels off — maybe a phrase sounds too stiff, or the letter mentions a skill you don't actually have. Tell ChatGPT exactly what to change, and a new version will appear.

What you'll see: your follow-up message goes into the text box, and a revised draft replaces the old one below it. Each round of feedback tightens the letter. If the draft is completely off-track, you can ask ChatGPT to start over with **"Let's try again — focus more on [specific thing]."**

💬 Example: *"The second paragraph sounds too formal — can you make it sound more like a real person talking? Also, please add one sentence about my volunteer work teaching kids to code."*

You'll know it worked when the draft feels closer to your own voice and only mentions things you've actually done.

## Step 5 — Move the draft into your own document

Once the draft is close to right, **copy it out of ChatGPT** and paste it into a Word document, Google Doc, or plain text file. Working in your own editor makes the next step — the rewriting — much easier than editing inside the chat.

If copying is awkward on mobile, look for a **share or copy icon** at the corner of the chat reply, or just select the text with your finger and copy. You can also email the draft to yourself from the chat.

💬 Example: Paste it into a Google Doc and rename the file **"[Job title] — cover letter — [your name]"** so it's easy to find later.

You'll know it worked when the letter is open in your own editor, separate from the chat, and you can edit it freely without losing the original.

## Step 6 — Rewrite parts in your own voice

This is the step that turns a ChatGPT draft into *your* cover letter. **Read every sentence out loud.** If you wouldn't actually say it that way to a real person, change the words. Replace any phrase that feels like a machine wrote it — usually the openings ("I am writing to express…") and the closings ("Thank you for your consideration…") — with something you'd really say.

You don't have to rewrite the whole letter. Often, just changing the first sentence and the last one is enough to make it sound like you. **One honest rule:** never claim experience the assistant invented. If a sentence mentions a skill you don't actually have, delete it — recruiters notice.

💬 Example: Change *"I am writing to express my interest in the position of Project Manager at your company"* to *"When I saw your opening for a Project Manager, it felt like a natural next step for me — here's why."*

You'll know it worked when you could imagine saying each sentence out loud in an interview without flinching, and every claim in the letter is something you've actually done.

## Common mistakes
- **Pasting the job post without telling ChatGPT what to focus on.** The result is a generic letter. **Fix:** always end your prompt with a short sentence about which strengths to highlight and what tone you want.
- **Letting the assistant invent experience.** If your background summary is vague, ChatGPT may confidently make up skills you don't have. **Fix:** mention only things you've actually done, and delete any line in the draft that doesn't match your real experience.
- **Sending the first draft as-is.** Recruiters can spot a robotic cover letter in seconds. **Fix:** always rewrite at least the first and last paragraph, so the letter sounds like a real person wrote it.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** the same prompt style works for **volunteer applications, scholarship essays, or short personal statements** — any time you need a tailored first draft from a long description and your own background.
- **For your work:** when you're job hunting, this approach lets you apply to **more roles in less time**, because each tailored draft only takes a few minutes instead of an hour.
- **If you're just getting started:** pick **one job** you've already saved, paste the post into ChatGPT with three sentences about yourself, and ask for a one-paragraph version. A short letter is the easiest way to learn how the tool responds before you commit to a longer one.

## Try it now
Pick one job posting you've been meaning to apply for. Open ChatGPT, paste the post plus a three-sentence summary of your background, and ask for a **one-paragraph cover letter draft**. Read it once, change the first sentence to something you'd actually say, and you're done — your first tailored draft, in under ten minutes.
